title: Avatar Workshop (1 class)
summary: Give a voice agent a face, then give it a job. Learn where businesses use avatars, talk to a live one in the browser, and turn it into a front desk for your own business: Deepgram listens, thinks and speaks, and SpatialReal animates a photoreal face. Nothing to install.
detail: A short talk on where avatars earn their keep. Everyone adds their own Deepgram and SpatialReal keys and talks to a live avatar that interviews them, and the room sees the totals. Then each person gives the avatar a job: a business name, what it should know and a personality, and the room tries to break it. The SpatialReal team shows how the face is made and what it costs. Then everyone learns how to put their avatar on their own website. 90 minutes, with drinks and snacks (no dinner).
outcome: A front-desk avatar for your own business that you built and tested, a sense of where avatars help and where they don't, and a page you can come back to with your own keys.
prereqs: Wired headphones, not speakers — on speakers the avatar talks to itself.
A Deepgram API key from console.deepgram.com. New accounts get credit, no card needed.
A SpatialReal API key and App ID from app.spatialreal.ai (Apps → Create API Key). The free tier covers the workshop.
artifact: A front-desk avatar for the attendee’s own business, running in the browser on their own keys.

slides.title: Voice-powered avatars
bullets: dgeventhub.com/lessons
slides.note: Play the Husk IRL video on the big screen while people arrive. Read the Wi-Fi password out loud; it is not published because this page is readable without an event code.

slides.title: Why put a face on a voice agent?
bullets: People look at faces: a screen with a face gets attention a waveform does not
Seeing lips move helps people follow speech in a loud room
A face sets the tone — calm for a clinic, upbeat for a store
It makes a screen feel staffed when nobody is free
slides.note: The face is not the intelligence. The listening, thinking and speaking are the same voice agent; the avatar is how it shows up on a screen.

slides.title: Where avatars earn their keep
bullets: Front desks and kiosks: hotels, clinic check-in, offices, event booths
Training and role-play: sales calls, job interviews, hard conversations
Tutoring and language practice
Support on a website or in an app
Internal help desks: HR, IT, new-hire onboarding
slides.note: Ask the room which one their company could use. The common thread: a person would otherwise be standing at a screen, waiting or repeating the same answers.

slides.title: When to skip the face
bullets: Phone calls — there is no screen, so use a plain voice agent
When every fraction of a second or cent matters
When people need to read, not watch: forms, code, long numbers
When a human must answer: diagnoses, legal or money decisions
slides.note: Same voice agent either way. The face is an add-on, not the brain.

slides.title: What you need
bullets: A laptop with Chrome, and wired headphones (not speakers)
A Deepgram key — console.deepgram.com
A SpatialReal API key + App ID — app.spatialreal.ai → Apps
Nothing to install, and no other keys
slides.note: Deepgram's Voice Agent does the listening, thinking and speaking on the Deepgram key, so nobody needs an LLM key of their own.

slides.title: Who's in the room?
bullets: Your interview answers, added up live
No names, just the room
slides.note: Put the Who's in the room panel (top of this page, set to Tonight) on the big screen and read out the highlights: how people heard about tonight, coding levels, what they want avatars for.

slides.title: Your avatar, your business
bullets: In the runner above, switch Character to "Your business"
Business name: real, or one you make up
What it should know: hours, prices, the questions people always ask
A personality, if you like
Press Start and be its first customer
slides.note: About 20 minutes. Same keys, same face. The only change is three boxes of text, which is the point: the job lives in the words, not the code.

slides.title: Does the voice fit the face?
bullets: Pick a voice that clashes with your face and talk for a minute
Now pick one that fits
Which would you trust at a front desk?
slides.note: Tone is half the experience. A calm clinic and a busy coffee shop want different voices on the same face.

slides.title: Try to break it
bullets: Volunteers to the big screen
Ask it something it was never told
Interrupt it, change the subject, ask for a discount
Did it hold up? What would you add to its facts?
slides.note: Then two or three people show their business avatar to the room. Every miss is a line to add to What it should know.

slides.title: Put it on your website
bullets: Pick Your business, fill it in, press Download my avatar
Open github.com/saccoface/avatar-website-starter and press Deploy to Render
Paste your two keys and your avatar file: you get a live web address
Add it to your site as a page or a box on any page
slides.note: Your keys stay on the server, never in the visitor's browser. The starter has limits built in (2 visitors at once, 5 minutes each) so a busy page can't run up a bill. Free Render sleeps when idle, so the first visit can take about a minute to wake.

flow.title: Sit down and try it
flow.note: Nothing to install. Paste your SpatialReal and Deepgram keys, pick a face and press Start. The avatar interviews you for a couple of minutes, so you get a feel for how it looks, sounds and keeps up, and whether you would use one. Your answers, without names, join the room totals at the top of the page. Later you come back here to give the avatar a job: switch Character to Your business.

troubleshooting: The avatar talks to itself: you are on speakers. Switch to wired headphones.
The avatar appears for a second, then vanishes: the free SpatialReal tier allows 2 sessions at once. Close other tabs running an avatar and press Start again.
SpatialReal needs both an API key and an App ID, and the App ID starts with app_. They sit side by side on the Apps page.
A key is rejected: copy it again, whole, with no spaces. A Deepgram key is 40 letters and numbers, not the dashed key ID shown in the list.
Sessions stop after 10 minutes on the free SpatialReal tier. Press Start again.
